description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/
summary: CLI-Anything wraps arbitrary desktop and server software into thin, JSON-emitting CLI harnesses built on Click, so any agent framework can drive them without a bespoke integration, and their CLI-Hub registry lets you `pip install` a wrapper for Calibre, Joplin, ArcGIS Pro, and dozens of other tools in one command. For someone juggling parallel agent sessions in PenguPool or pushing Claude and Codex from AgentOn Pocket, this is the composable, local-first glue layer I actually want: the agent talks to a CLI, the CLI talks to the app, and the structured output is something I can log, inspect, and trust instead of scraping a GUI. I appreciate the 2,400-test validation baseline far more than the "tomorrow's users are agents" tagline, but the engineering underneath is the kind of toil-removing abstraction that turns a pile of one-off MCP servers into something genuinely composable.
